prompt:
The table below shows the average number of minutes per day that teenagers in one country spent on four activities in 2005 and 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

samples.text:
The table gives information about the average amount of time that teenagers in one country spent each day on social media, reading for pleasure, sport and exercise, and homework in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, the time spent on social media increased dramatically, and it became the most popular activity in 2025. In contrast, teenagers spent less time on reading and sport, while homework stayed almost the same.

In 2005, teenagers used social media for only 15 minutes a day, which was the lowest of the four activities. By 2025, this figure had risen to 140 minutes, more than nine times higher.

Reading for pleasure and sport both fell during the period. Reading dropped from 45 to 20 minutes, and sport and exercise went down from 60 to 45 minutes. Homework was the activity with the most time in 2005, at 70 minutes, and it rose slightly to 75 minutes in 2025, so it was the second most common activity at the end.

samples.text:
The table compares how many minutes per day teenagers in one country devoted to four activities in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, the pattern of teenagers' time changed markedly. Social media, the least time-consuming activity in 2005, had become by far the most time-consuming by 2025, while reading for pleasure and sport declined and homework remained broadly stable.

The rise in social media use was dramatic. Teenagers spent just a quarter of an hour a day on it in 2005, but this had grown to 140 minutes, more than two hours, twenty years later, a roughly ninefold increase.

Over the same period, the two leisure activities that do not involve screens lost ground. Time spent reading for pleasure more than halved, from 45 to 20 minutes, making it the least time-consuming activity in 2025, and sport and exercise fell by a quarter, from 60 to 45 minutes. Homework, which had been the largest item in 2005 at 70 minutes, increased only marginally to 75 minutes, leaving it a distant second to social media.

summary.en: A sharp overview showing the reversal; flexible expression of data (a quarter of an hour, more than halved, fell by a quarter); clear cohesion and organisation.

samples.text:
The table shows the average daily time that teenagers in one country spent on four activities in 2005 and in 2025.

The most striking change is the rise of social media, which went from the smallest to the largest share of teenagers' time. Screen-free leisure, in the form of reading and sport, declined, whereas homework hardly changed.

In 2005, social media accounted for just 15 minutes a day, far less than any other activity. Twenty years later, teenagers were spending 140 minutes on it, around nine times as long. This was more than the combined time they spent reading for pleasure and doing sport in 2025 (65 minutes).

Both of those activities fell. Reading was hit hardest, dropping from 45 to 20 minutes and becoming the least time-consuming of the four, while sport and exercise decreased more moderately, from an hour to 45 minutes. Homework, the main demand on teenagers' time in 2005 at 70 minutes, edged up to 75 minutes but was overtaken comfortably by social media.

samples.text:
The table sets out how many minutes a day, on average, teenagers in one country spent on four activities in 2005 and 2025.

Over these two decades, social media moved from the margins to the centre of teenagers' days, becoming by far their most time-consuming activity. Reading and sport both lost time, while homework stayed almost constant.

The scale of the change in social media use is remarkable. In 2005 it occupied a mere 15 minutes daily, the smallest figure in the table; by 2025 it took up 140 minutes, roughly nine times as much and more than reading and sport put together.

The declines were uneven. Reading for pleasure more than halved, from 45 to 20 minutes, falling from third place to last, whereas sport and exercise lost a quarter of its time, slipping from 60 to 45 minutes. Homework, which had demanded more time than anything else in 2005 (70 minutes), rose by just five minutes, so that by 2025 teenagers were spending nearly twice as long on social media as on their schoolwork.

summary.vi: Hoàn chỉnh: tổng quan bằng hình ảnh ('from the margins to the centre'), mọi so sánh chính xác (gần gấp đôi bài tập: 140 vs 75), ngôn ngữ tinh tế, tự nhiên và chính xác tuyệt đối.
summary.en: Complete: a vivid overview ('from the margins to the centre'), every comparison accurate (nearly twice homework: 140 vs 75), sophisticated, natural and fully accurate language.
summary.ja: 完璧：比喩的な概要（'from the margins to the centre'）、全ての比較が正確（宿題のほぼ2倍：140対75）、洗練され自然で完全に正確な言語。
summary.ru: Безупречно: образный обзор ('from the margins to the centre'), все сравнения точны (почти вдвое больше, чем на домашние задания: 140 против 75), изысканный, естественный и абсолютно точный язык.
